summary: Al-Akhirah refers to everything that follows this worldly life — the Day of Judgement, the reckoning of deeds, and the eternal destinations of Paradise and Hell. Belief in the afterlife is one of the six articles of faith.
content:
Al-Akhirah (the Hereafter) encompasses everything that follows death and the end of the world: the resurrection of all creation, the gathering on the Day of Judgement, the weighing of deeds, the crossing of the Sirat (bridge), and the final destinations of Jannah (Paradise) and Jahannam (Hell). Belief in the Hereafter is the sixth of the six articles of faith and is foundational to the Islamic worldview.

The Quran mentions the Hereafter hundreds of times and consistently pairs it with belief in Allah: those who truly believe in Allah live with awareness of accountability. Allah says: 'Every soul shall taste death. Then to Us you will be returned' (29:57).

## Signs of the Hour

Islamic theology distinguishes between minor signs (ashrat as-sa'ah as-sughra) — those which have appeared and those which continue to emerge — and major signs (ashrat as-sa'ah al-kubra), which signal the imminent arrival of the Day of Judgement.

The major signs, narrated in authentic hadith, include:

1. **The Dajjal (the Antichrist)** — a great trial for humanity, the greatest fitnah (tribulation) since creation (Muslim 2946)
2. **The descent of Isa (Jesus)** — he will descend near Damascus, break the cross, kill the Dajjal, and establish justice (Muslim 2937)
3. **Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog)** — their release after Isa's descent (Muslim 2937)
4. **Three great earthquakes (khusuf)** — in the east, west, and Arabian Peninsula
5. **The smoke (dukhan)** — a smoke that will cover the earth
6. **The rising of the sun from the west** — after which repentance is no longer accepted (Bukhari 4635)
7. **The Beast (al-Dabbah)** — which will emerge and mark people
8. **A fire from Yemen** — driving people to the place of gathering
9. **The destruction of the Ka'bah** by a man with thin legs from Abyssinia (Bukhari 1591)
10. **The disappearance of the Quran from hearts and written copies**

## The Day of Judgement (Yawm al-Qiyamah)

On this day — the length of which is described as fifty thousand years for some, or shorter for the believers through Allah's mercy (70:4) — all of creation will be resurrected and gathered. Every person will be shown their book of deeds: 'So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it' (99:7-8).

The scales (al-mizan) will weigh deeds with perfect justice. No soul will be wronged in the slightest. The Prophet (peace be upon him) will intercede for the believers — this is the Maqam al-Mahmud, the praised station promised to him (17:79).

The Sirat — a bridge over Jahannam — must be crossed. People cross it according to their deeds: some like lightning, some running, some crawling, and some falling into the Fire.

## Jannah — Paradise

Jannah is the eternal abode of the righteous. The Quran describes rivers of water, milk, honey, and wine (of the type that causes no harm), gardens beneath which rivers flow, and a life free from all grief, fatigue, and death. The greatest blessing of Jannah is the vision of Allah: 'Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord' (75:22-23).

Jannah has levels, with Firdaws al-A'la (the highest) at the top: the Prophet (peace be upon him) encouraged asking Allah for al-Firdaws (Bukhari 2790). Entry into Jannah is ultimately by Allah's mercy, not by deeds alone (Bukhari 6467).

## Jahannam — Hell

Jahannam is the abode of punishment for those who rejected faith and died upon disbelief, and a place of temporary punishment for sinful believers according to their deeds. The Quran describes its fire, its chains, its intense heat, and its custodians (angels).

Regarding believers who enter the Fire: the consensus of Ahl us-Sunnah is that they will eventually be removed and admitted to Jannah by Allah's mercy or by the intercession of the Prophet and others whom Allah permits to intercede. Only the disbelievers will remain therein forever.

## The Barzakh — The Interval

Between death and resurrection lies the Barzakh, the intermediate realm. In the grave, the deceased will be questioned by Munkar and Nakir about their Lord, their religion, and their Prophet. Those who answer correctly will experience comfort; those who cannot will experience distress. The punishment and blessing of the grave (adhab al-qabr and ni'mat al-qabr) are established in authentic hadith and affirmed by Ahl us-Sunnah.
evidence_quran: Surah al-Ankabut 29:57 — 'Every soul shall taste death. Then to Us you will be returned'
Surah al-Zalzalah 99:7-8 — 'Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it'
Surah al-Qiyamah 75:22-23 — 'Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord'
Surah al-Ma'arij 70:4 — 'The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a day the extent of which is fifty thousand years'
Surah al-Isra 17:79 — '...that your Lord may raise you to a praised station'
evidence_hadith: Muslim 2946 — Hadith of Dajjal as the greatest fitnah since creation
Muslim 2937 — Hadith of the descent of Isa and the major signs
Bukhari 4635 — Rising of the sun from the west; repentance no longer accepted after it
Bukhari 6467 — 'None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds'; the companions said: Not even you? He said: Not even me, unless Allah covers me with His mercy
scholar_positions: The major signs of the Hour are affirmed by Ahl us-Sunnah based on sahih hadith. The Athari position affirms the physical reality of Jannah, Jahannam, the Sirat, the Mizan, and the vision of Allah without metaphorical reinterpretation. Ash'ari and Maturidi scholars agree on all these realities; minor differences in framing certain descriptions do not affect the core creed. The intercession of the Prophet (shafa'ah) is affirmed by all three schools and rejected by the Mu'tazilah.
sources: Ibn Kathir, al-Nihayah fi al-Fitan wa al-Malahim
Ibn al-Qayyim, Hadi al-Arwah ila Bilad al-Afrah (description of Jannah)
al-Nawawi, Sharh Muslim (commentary on hadith of major signs)
al-Tahawiyyah al-Aqeedah — Imam al-Tahawi, commentary by Ibn Abi al-Izz
